package: @astryxdesign/core
## Focus

# useCombobox

Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.

## Import

```tsx
import { useCombobox } from '@astryxdesign/core/Selector';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and set the control's `aria-activedescendant` only while `isOpen` and `highlightedIndex` points at a rendered option, as CommandPalette does.
- **Do:** For type-to-select without a search field, run useTypeahead's handler first and fall through to this `onKeyDown` when it returns false, as Selector does.
- **Do:** For a field you render, spread the prop getters, and set the active option yourself when a new query changes the options: the first option so Enter picks it, or -1 so Enter stays the field’s.
- **Do:** Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query (AST-075 DEC-2). When nothing matches, announce the words the field shows for it.
- **Don't:** Render controls that are not options, such as a create button or an empty message, inside the listbox; render them beside it.
- **Don't:** Move DOM focus onto the options; the active option is announced through `aria-activedescendant` while focus stays on the control.

## Accessibility

- **Focus stays in the field:** With the prop getters, moving the active option never moves focus out of the field. The field names the active option through `aria-activedescendant` and carries none while no option is active.
- **Expanded state follows the list:** While the listbox renders, the field exposes `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` naming it. Otherwise it exposes `aria-expanded="false"` and references nothing.
- **Roles:** The field is a `combobox` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected="true"` on the active one. You name the field and the listbox.
- **Keys:** While the list shows, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active option and wrap; Enter picks an active option and only then stops the field’s own Enter; Escape, whatever modifier is held, hides the list without closing an enclosing dialog or popover on the same press. While it is hidden, ArrowDown shows it when there are options. An open field with no options still takes Escape, which closes the list, so render an empty message while it is open. Home, End, other chords such as Shift+Enter, and every other key reach the field.
- **Input method:** No key moves, picks or hides while an input method is composing text.
- **Pointer:** Moving the pointer over an option makes it active without moving focus; pressing an option picks it, and the field keeps focus through the press.
- **Result count:** Yours to announce: compose useAnnounce (AST-075 DEC-2) so each new query announces the number of options, or that there are none, once and politely. For none, announce the words the field shows.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseComboboxOptions` | - | Configuration object. **(required)** |
| `options.selectableItems` | `ReadonlyArray<T extends {value: string; disabled?: boolean}>` | - | The options in the same order as they render: `SelectorOptionData`, or any option type with a string `value` and an optional `disabled`. Options with `disabled` cannot be picked and are skipped while moving through the open list; ArrowDown or ArrowUp that opens the list from `onKeyDown` lands on the selected option when it is enabled, else on the first or last enabled option. **(required)** |
| `options.isOpen` | `boolean` | - | Whether the list is shown. The caller owns this state. **(required)** |
| `options.onOpen` | `() => unknown` | - | Called to show the list. Return `false` to refuse; the hook then leaves the highlight alone. **(required)** |
| `options.onClose` | `() => void` | - | Called when the hook hides the list; the hook resets the highlight first. When the caller closes the list itself (an outside press, say), it should also call `setHighlightedIndex(-1)`. **(required)** |
| `options.listboxId` | `string` | - | The listbox element's id. Option ids are derived from it through `getItemId`. **(required)** |
| `options.value` | `string` | - | The selected value. Opening the list highlights it when it is enabled; otherwise ArrowUp opens on the last enabled option and ArrowDown, a press, Enter or Space on the first. A disabled option is never highlighted on opening, and with no enabled option nothing is. |
| `options.onSelect` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the picked value. Picking also closes the list. |
| `options.onClear` | `() => void` | - | Clears the value. When provided, Delete or Backspace on the closed control clears it, so clearing is not pointer-only. Ignored while the list is open or with `hasSearch`. |
| `options.hasSearch` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the list has its own search field. Space then types instead of picking, opening by a press or Enter does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the selected or the first or last enabled option), and printable keys on the closed control go to `onSearchSeed`. |
| `options.onSearchSeed` | `(char: string) => void` | - | With `hasSearch`, receives each printable character except Space typed while the control has focus, opening the list first when it is closed, so type-to-find needs no separate open step. |
| `options.isDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the control ignores clicks and keys. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `highlightedIndex` | `number` | Index of the active option, or -1 when none is active. With `hasSearch`, opening by a press or Enter does not set one, so it stays -1 after the hook itself closes the list; ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the selected or the first or last enabled option. Render it as the active option and name it in `aria-activedescendant` only while it points at a rendered option. |
| `setHighlightedIndex` | `(index: number) => void` | Sets the active option, for example from a filter that changes the options. |
| `getItemId` | `(index: number) => string` | The id to render on the option at `index`. Set the control's `aria-activedescendant` to `isOpen && highlightedIndex >= 0 && highlightedIndex < selectableItems.length ? getItemId(highlightedIndex) : undefined`, so it never names an option that does not exist, including in an empty list. |
| `onTriggerClick` | `() => void` | Toggles the list from a press on the control. |
| `onKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | Key handler for the control that keeps focus. ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active option; Enter (and Space without search) picks it or opens the list; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option. An editable control that keeps Home and End for the caret does not pass them to this handler, as CommandPalette does. |
| `onItemSelect` | `(item: T) => void` | Picks an option from a press on it, then closes the list. |
| `onItemMouseEnter` | `(item: T, index: number) => void` | Makes the hovered option active without scrolling the list or moving focus. |
| `getFieldProps` | `(props?: {onKeyDown?(event: React.KeyboardEvent): void}) => object` | Props for a single-line `input` you render: `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls` only while the listbox renders (`isOpen` with at least one option), `aria-activedescendant` only while an option is active, and the field’s key handler. Pass your own `onKeyDown` here rather than beside the spread: it runs after the hook’s handler unless that handler claimed the key, and it may be typed for its element. |
| `getListboxProps` | `() => object` | Props for the listbox you render, anywhere in the document, including the page’s flow: its `id` and `role`, and a press handler that keeps focus in the field. Render it while `isOpen` and there are options, and name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `getOptionProps` | `(index: number) => object` | Props for the option at `index`: its `id`, `role`, `aria-selected` (true on the active option), `aria-disabled` on a disabled one, a pointer move that makes it active without moving focus, and a press that picks it. |

## Related

Components: Selector, CommandPalette
Hooks: useMultiCombobox, useTypeahead, useAnnounce

# useFocusTrap

Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.

## Import

```tsx
import { useFocusTrap } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Call focusFirst() when opening a dialog/modal to move focus into the trapped region.
- **Do:** Provide an onEscape callback to close the dialog when Escape is pressed.
- **Do:** Rely on the built-in focus restoration on close; only add your own onHide focus handling when you need to send focus somewhere other than the previously-focused element.
- **Don't:** Use on non-modal content like tooltips or dropdowns; those need light-dismiss, not focus trapping.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseFocusTrapOptions` | - | Configuration object for the focus trap. **(required)** |
| `options.isActive` | `boolean` | - | Whether the focus trap is currently active. **(required)** |
| `options.onEscape` | `() => void` | - | Callback when Escape key is pressed inside the trapped container. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `containerRef` | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | Ref to attach to the container element that should trap focus. |
| `focusFirst` | `() => void` | Focuses the first focusable element inside the container. |

## Related

Components: Dialog, DatePicker
Hooks: useListFocus, useScrollLock

# useGridFocus

Manages keyboard navigation within a 2D grid following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, and Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g., month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.

## Import

```tsx
import { useGridFocus } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Use for calendar date grids: wire onPageUp/onPageDown to month navigation and onNavigateBefore/onNavigateAfter for cross-month arrow key navigation.
- **Do:** Attach both gridRef and handleKeyDown to the grid container element.
- **Do:** For roving-tabindex grids (e.g. Calendar), set hasRovingTabIndex: true and attach handleFocus to the container onFocus; seed one focus target with tabindex=0 and the hook repairs and moves it.
- **Don't:** Use for simple linear lists; prefer useListFocus for 1D navigation.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseGridFocusOptions` | - | Configuration object for grid focus behavior. **(required)** |
| `options.columns` | `number` | - | Number of columns in the grid. Used for up/down navigation (moves by this many cells). **(required)** |
| `options.cellSelector` | `string` | `'button:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'` | Selector for cells within the grid. Should match ALL cell positions in DOM order (including disabled/empty) so grid geometry is preserved. |
| `options.isCellFocusable` | `(cell: HTMLElement) => boolean` | - | Predicate for whether a matched cell can receive focus. Omit to treat every matched cell as focusable. |
| `options.getFocusTarget` | `(cell: HTMLElement) => HTMLElement \| null` | - | Resolves the element to focus for a cell, e.g. a button inside a role="gridcell" wrapper. Omit to focus the cell itself. |
| `options.onNavigateBefore` | `(column: number, offset: number) => void` | - | Callback when navigation would go before the first cell. Receives the column index and offset (1 for horizontal, columns for vertical). |
| `options.onNavigateAfter` | `(column: number, offset: number) => void` | - | Callback when navigation would go after the last cell. Receives the column index and offset. |
| `options.onPageUp` | `(event: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | - | Callback for Page Up key (e.g., navigate to previous month in calendars). Receives the key event, so `event.shiftKey` can select a larger step, such as a year. |
| `options.onPageDown` | `(event: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | - | Callback for Page Down key (e.g., navigate to next month in calendars). Receives the key event, so `event.shiftKey` can select a larger step, such as a year. |
| `options.hasRovingTabIndex` | `boolean` | `false` | Own a single roving tab stop across the grid: one focusable cell (its resolved focus target) carries tabindex="0", the rest -1. Stamped/repaired on render and moved with arrow navigation. Attach the returned handleFocus to the container onFocus. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `gridRef` | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | Ref to attach to the grid container element. |
| `handleKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | Key down handler to attach to the grid container. |
| `handleFocus` | `(e: React.FocusEvent) => void` | Focus handler for the grid container. Keeps the roving tab stop in sync when hasRovingTabIndex is enabled; a no-op otherwise, so always safe to attach. |
| `focusCell` | `(index: number) => void` | Focus a specific cell by index (clamped to valid range). |
| `focusFirst` | `() => void` | Focus the first focusable cell in the grid. |
| `focusLast` | `() => void` | Focus the last focusable cell in the grid. |

## Related

Components: Calendar
Hooks: useListFocus, useFocusTrap

# useIndicatorFocusRing

Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.

## Import

```tsx
import { useIndicatorFocusRing } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Wrap only the indicator in the ref'd element; a wrapper holding label text would ring the whole row.
- **Do:** Spread focusProps on the element that contains the hidden input, not on the input itself.
- **Don't:** Ask a themeable indicator to draw its own focus ring; a replacement that ignores the prop leaves the control with no visible focus.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `containerRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | - | Ref to an element wrapping only the indicator, so its single element child is unambiguously the thing to ring. **(required)** |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Skip the ring; a disabled control is not focusable. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `focusProps` | `{onFocus: (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void; onBlur: () => void}` | Spread onto the element that owns the focusable input. |

## Related

Components: CheckboxInput, RadioList, Selector
Hooks: useFocusTrap

# useKeyboardHint

Shows an ephemeral "← → to navigate" hint anchored to the focused item the first time a roving-tabindex composite (Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl, etc.) receives keyboard focus. It teaches sighted keyboard users that arrow keys move within the group. The hint renders arrow keys with Kbd in the top layer (popover="manual") and is CSS-anchor-positioned to the focused element, so overflow containers never clip it. It auto-dismisses on the first arrow press, on timeout, or on blur, and does not re-show for that instance. Toolbar, TabList, and SegmentedControl wire this in automatically; reach for the hook directly only when building a custom roving-tabindex widget.

## Import

```tsx
import { useKeyboardHint } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Compose the returned onFocus/onKeyDown with your existing focus handlers rather than replacing them: call onKeyDown first (it only dismisses, never prevents), then your navigation handler.
- **Do:** Render hintElement as the last child of the composite container; it is position:fixed in the top layer and aria-hidden, so it never affects layout or the accessibility tree.
- **Do:** Match orientation to the arrow keys your widget actually responds to so the hint shows the correct icons.
- **Don't:** Use for single controls or widgets without roving-tabindex navigation; the hint only makes sense where arrows move focus within a group.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseKeyboardHintOptions` | - | Configuration object for the keyboard hint. |
| `options.orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical' \| 'both'` | `'horizontal'` | Which arrow-key axis the composite navigates, controlling which arrow icons the hint shows (← → for horizontal, ↑ ↓ for vertical, all four for both). |
| `options.dismissAfterMs` | `number` | `3000` | Milliseconds before the hint auto-dismisses after appearing. |
| `options.isEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the hint is enabled. Set to false to suppress it for a specific instance (e.g. a disabled or read-only widget). |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `hintElement` | `ReactNode` | The popover hint element to render inside the composite container (as the last child). Portals to the top layer via popover="manual", renders arrow keys with Kbd, and manages its own visibility; render it unconditionally. |
| `onFocus` | `(e: React.FocusEvent) => void` | Attach to the container onFocus. Shows the hint on the first keyboard-focus (:focus-visible) entry from outside the composite. |
| `onBlur` | `(e: React.FocusEvent) => void` | Attach to the container onBlur. Hides the hint when focus leaves the composite entirely, and re-anchors when focus moves within. |
| `onKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | Attach to the container onKeyDown. Dismisses the hint on the first arrow press (the user has discovered the interaction). Never prevents default or stops propagation. |

## Related

Components: Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl
Hooks: useListFocus, useGridFocus, useTreeFocus

# useListFocus

Manages keyboard navigation within a linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical, horizontal, or both), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, RTL, and Escape to close. Opt into hasRovingTabIndex for composite widgets (toolbars, segmented controls, tab strips) that own a single tab stop. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, and any 1D focusable list.

## Import

```tsx
import { useListFocus } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Set orientation to 'horizontal' for toolbars and tab bars, 'vertical' for dropdown menus.
- **Do:** Provide an onEscape callback for menus/dropdowns to return focus to the trigger.
- **Do:** Enable hasRovingTabIndex (and hasCaretGuard when the widget can contain text inputs) for toolbar-style composites that should be a single tab stop.
- **Don't:** Use for 2D grid navigation; prefer useGridFocus for grids and calendars.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseListFocusOptions` | - | Configuration object for list focus behavior. All fields are optional. |
| `options.itemSelector` | `string` | `'[role="menuitem"]'` | Selector for focusable items within the list. |
| `options.boundarySelector` | `string` | - | Selector identifying a list boundary, for lists that contain nested lists of the same kind (e.g. a menu with submenu flyouts). When set, item collection and key handling are scoped to this level's own container. Typically '[role="menu"]'. |
| `options.wrap` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether arrow navigation wraps around at the ends. |
| `options.onEscape` | `() => void` | - | Callback when Escape key is pressed (e.g., close menu). Supplying it also consumes the key (preventDefault); without it Escape passes through to the surrounding layer. |
| `options.orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | Navigation orientation. 'horizontal' uses ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, 'vertical' uses ArrowUp/ArrowDown, 'both' accepts all four arrows. |
| `options.hasHomeEnd` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether Home/End jump to the first/last enabled item. |
| `options.hasPaging` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether PageDown/PageUp page through a scrolling list: PageDown moves to the last enabled item fully visible in the container, and pressed there again one viewport further; PageUp mirrors it. Neither wraps; in a list that does not scroll they act as End/Home. |
| `options.hasRovingTabIndex` | `boolean` | `false` | Opt into roving-tabindex ownership: the hook stamps a single tab stop (one item tabindex="0", the rest -1), repairs it as items mount/unmount or toggle disabled, and moves it with arrow navigation. When false, the hook only moves focus and never touches tabindex. |
| `options.hasCaretGuard` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, arrow keys are not stolen from a nested text input/textarea whose caret is not at the boundary in the direction of travel (or that has a selection), and are never stolen from a nested contenteditable (rich-text editor / chat composer). Preserves inline text editing within the list. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `listRef` | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | Ref to attach to the list container element. |
| `handleKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | Key down handler to attach to the list container. |
| `handleFocus` | `(e: React.FocusEvent) => void` | Focus handler for the container. Keeps the roving tab stop in sync when hasRovingTabIndex is enabled; a no-op otherwise, so it is always safe to attach. |
| `focusItem` | `(index: number) => void` | Focus a specific item by index (clamped to valid range). |
| `focusFirst` | `() => boolean` | Focus the first enabled item. Returns true when an item was focused. |
| `focusLast` | `() => boolean` | Focus the last enabled item. Returns true when an item was focused. |
| `ownsEvent` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => boolean` | Whether a key event belongs to this list level rather than a nested list sharing the same boundarySelector. Always true when no boundarySelector is set. Use to guard consumer-added key handling (Enter/Space, typeahead). |
| `getItems` | `() => HTMLElement[]` | This level's focusable items in DOM order (already scoped by boundarySelector). Build typeahead targets from this instead of re-querying. |

## Related

Components: TabMenu, Toolbar
Hooks: useGridFocus, useFocusTrap

# useMultiCombobox

Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.

## Import

```tsx
import { useMultiCombobox } from '@astryxdesign/core/MultiSelector';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and pass `activeDescendantId` as the control's `aria-activedescendant`.
- **Do:** Use `isGrid` only when rows carry a control next to the option; give each action cell `id={getActionCellId(index)}`.
- **Do:** Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query.
- **Don't:** Close the list after each toggle; a multi-select stays open so several options can be picked in a row.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseMultiComboboxOptions` | - | Configuration object. **(required)** |
| `options.selectableItems` | `MultiSelectorOptionData[]` | - | The options in the same order as they render. Options with `disabled` cannot be toggled and are skipped while moving through the open list. Opening never lands on a disabled option: ArrowUp opens on the last enabled option, and ArrowDown, a press, Enter or Space on the first enabled option. **(required)** |
| `options.isOpen` | `boolean` | - | Whether the list is shown. The caller owns this state. **(required)** |
| `options.onOpen` | `() => unknown` | - | Called to show the list. Return `false` to refuse; the hook then leaves the highlight alone. **(required)** |
| `options.onClose` | `() => void` | - | Called to hide the list. The highlight resets first. **(required)** |
| `options.onToggle` | `(itemValue: string) => void` | - | Called with the value of the option to add or remove. Toggling keeps the list open. **(required)** |
| `options.listboxId` | `string` | - | The listbox (or grid) element's id. Option and action-cell ids are derived from it. **(required)** |
| `options.hasSearch` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the list has its own search field. Space then types instead of toggling, opening by a press or Enter does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the first and last enabled option), Delete and Backspace edit the query, and type-to-select is off. Home and End still jump to the first and last option, so a search input that keeps them for the caret should stop them before this handler and rely on PageUp and PageDown. |
| `options.onClear` | `() => void` | - | Clears every selected value. When provided, Delete or Backspace on the closed control clears them, so clearing is not pointer-only. Ignored while the list is open or with `hasSearch`. |
| `options.hasValue` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether anything is selected. The Delete and Backspace clear is skipped when false. |
| `options.isGrid` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether each row pairs an option cell with an action cell. The inline-end arrow then moves the highlight to the row's action and the inline-start arrow back, following visual direction in right-to-left layouts, and Enter on the action runs `onActivateAction` instead of toggling. |
| `options.rowHasAction` | `(index: number) => boolean` | - | In a grid, whether the row at `index` has an action cell to move to. |
| `options.onActivateAction` | `(index: number) => void` | - | In a grid, runs the control in the highlighted row's action cell. The selection does not change. |
| `options.isDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the control ignores clicks and keys. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `highlightedIndex` | `number` | Index of the active row, or -1 when none is active. |
| `setHighlightedIndex` | `(index: number) => void` | Sets the active row, for example after filtering. The highlight lands on the row's option cell. |
| `highlightedCell` | `'option' \| 'action'` | Which cell of the active row is highlighted; `'action'` only in a grid. |
| `activeDescendantId` | `string \| undefined` | The id to pass as the control's `aria-activedescendant`: the active option, or its action cell in a grid. Undefined while the list is closed or nothing is active. |
| `getItemId` | `(index: number) => string` | The id to render on the option at `index`. |
| `getActionCellId` | `(index: number) => string` | In a grid, the id to render on the action cell of row `index`. |
| `onTriggerClick` | `() => void` | Toggles the list from a press on the control. |
| `onKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | Key handler for the control that keeps focus. ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active row; Enter (and Space without search) toggles the active option and keeps the list open; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option; without search, typed characters move to the next option whose label starts with them, as in Selector (a repeated letter cycles, and a single letter searches from the option after the active one), and Space still toggles. |
| `onItemMouseEnter` | `(item: MultiSelectorOptionData, index: number, cell?: 'option' \| 'action') => void` | Makes the hovered option, or its action cell, active without scrolling the list or moving focus. |

## Related

Components: MultiSelector

# useTreeFocus

Manages roving-tabindex focus and the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model. ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End roam linearly over the visible treeitems (skipping disabled ones), while ArrowRight/ArrowLeft carry tree semantics (expand/collapse, move to first-child/parent). Enter/Space activate, and printable characters trigger typeahead.

## Import

```tsx
import { useTreeFocus } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Use for hierarchical tree widgets: wire onToggleExpand to your expansion state and onActiveChange to a single roving tab stop.
- **Do:** Attach both treeRef and handleKeyDown to the role="tree" container element.
- **Don't:** Use for linear lists (prefer useListFocus) or 2D grids (prefer useGridFocus); those traversals differ from a tree.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseTreeFocusOptions` | - | Configuration object for tree focus behavior. |
| `options.itemSelector` | `string` | `'[role="treeitem"]'` | Selector for visible treeitems within the tree, in DOM order. |
| `options.isItemDisabled` | `(item: HTMLElement) => boolean` | - | Predicate for whether a treeitem is disabled and must be skipped during navigation. Defaults to reading `data-tree-disabled` / `aria-disabled`. |
| `options.getLevel` | `(item: HTMLElement) => number` | - | Reads the 1-based nesting level of a treeitem. Defaults to the `aria-level` attribute. |
| `options.onToggleExpand` | `(id: string) => void` | - | Called to expand/collapse the treeitem with the given id (ArrowRight on a collapsed parent, ArrowLeft on an expanded parent, Enter/Space on a parent without its own action). |
| `options.onActivate` | `(item: HTMLElement, id: string \| undefined) => boolean \| void` | - | Called when Enter/Space activates a treeitem. Return true when handled; return false/undefined to let the hook fall back to toggling expansion. |
| `options.onActiveChange` | `(id: string \| undefined) => void` | - | Notified when the hook moves focus to a treeitem. Consumers use this to move a single roving tab stop. |
| `options.hasRovingTabIndex` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, the hook owns a single roving tab stop across the visible treeitems (stamps tabindex 0/-1, repairs on mount, moves with navigation). Preserves an existing tabindex="0" seed on mount. Attach the returned `handleFocus` to keep the stop in sync after clicks. |
| `options.typeahead` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether typeahead (jump to next item whose text starts with the typed characters, ignoring case, accents, the stroked letters đ ł ø ħ ŧ ƀ and Turkish ı/İ in every locale) is enabled. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `treeRef` | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | Ref to attach to the tree container element (role="tree"). |
| `handleKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent) => void` | Key down handler to attach to the tree container. |
| `handleFocus` | `(e: React.FocusEvent) => void` | Focus handler to attach to the container's onFocus. Keeps the roving tab stop in sync when hasRovingTabIndex is enabled; a no-op otherwise, so always safe to attach. |
| `focusFirst` | `() => void` | Focus the first enabled visible treeitem. |
| `focusLast` | `() => void` | Focus the last enabled visible treeitem. |

# useTypeahead

Adds APG type-to-focus search to a collection: printable keystrokes are buffered (resetting after a pause), and the first item whose label starts with the buffer (ignoring case, accents, the stroked letters đ ł ø ħ ŧ ƀ and Turkish ı/İ, the same in every locale; a typed accent prefers the exact match) is reported through onMatch. Pressing the same letter repeatedly cycles through the matches rather than filtering deeper. It moves nothing itself; pair it with the collection's own focus management, most often useListFocus or useGridFocus.

## Import

```tsx
import { useTypeahead } from '@astryxdesign/core/hooks';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Wire onMatch to the focus manager you already have (useListFocus.focusItem) instead of moving focus yourself.
- **Do:** Let it see the key event first and fall through to arrow-key navigation only when it returns false.
- **Do:** Pass getCurrentIndex so repeated presses of one letter walk through matches instead of sticking on the first.
- **Don't:** Use it on a text input; the field already receives the characters, and typeahead would fight the value.

## Parameters

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | `UseTypeaheadOptions` | - | Configuration object. **(required)** |
| `options.getItemLabels` | `() => ReadonlyArray<string \| null \| undefined>` | - | Returns the item labels in DOM order. A null or empty entry marks a non-matchable slot and keeps indices aligned with the caller's items. **(required)** |
| `options.onMatch` | `(index: number) => void` | - | Called with the index of the matched item so the caller can focus or select it; typically useListFocus's focusItem. **(required)** |
| `options.getCurrentIndex` | `() => number` | `() => -1` | The index to search from, usually the focused item, so repeated presses of one letter cycle through matches. A negative value means nothing is current. |
| `options.resetMs` | `number` | `750` | Milliseconds of inactivity after which the typed buffer resets. |
| `options.isDisabled` | `(index: number) => boolean` | - | Whether an index should be skipped, e.g. disabled items. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `onKeyDown` | `(e: React.KeyboardEvent \| KeyboardEvent) => boolean` | Keydown handler. Returns true when it consumed a printable character, so the caller can stop its own key handling. |
| `reset` | `() => void` | Clears the pending buffer, e.g. when the collection closes. |
